BURHAN:v4p266/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p266/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p266/r1.claim: In 90:17, thumma marks the higher rank of faith relative to freeing and feeding, not later timing; the verse also adds believers' mutual counsel to patience and mercy.
BURHAN:v4p266/r1.anchor: دخلت لبيان تفاوت رتبة الفك والاطعام من رتبة الايمان إلا إن فيها زيادة تعرض لوصف المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v10p338/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p338/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p338/r10.claim: Fakk is separating one thing from another by removing it, as with a fetter; freeing a neck removes slavery, and “neck” denotes the whole enslaved person as “head” or “back” can denote a mount.
BURSEVI:v10p338/r10.anchor: الفك الفرق بين الشيئين بإزالة أحدهما عن الآخر كفك القيد والغل

BURSEVI:v10p339/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339/r10.claim: Emancipation and feeding are singled out because they are difficult: people readily spend on desires and surplus buildings but begrudge even a small gift or bite to an orphan or poor person whom they disdain.
BURSEVI:v10p339/r10.anchor: خص الفك والإطعام لصعوبة العمل بهما وجعل الإطعام لليتيم والمسكين لما إن ذلك يثقل على النفس

QASHANI:90:8-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:8-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:8-14/r3.claim: Freeing a neck means releasing the heart, imprisoned by ego-desire, through total detachment from natural inclinations; if that fails, one practices virtues until they become natural.
QASHANI:90:8-14/r3.anchor: تخليص رقبة القلب الأسير في قيد هوى النفس وفكها عن أسرها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r1.claim: Freeing a slave is the first virtue named, universally recognized as good and placed at the forefront of human service from the Qur’an’s earliest preaching; the Qur’an later promoted slavery’s gradual elimination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r1.anchor: Liberating a slave and making an effort that others also do so

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r1.claim: These readers use the verbal forms فك رقبة or أطعم, with رقبة in the accusative; Abū ʿAmr's transmitters report minor differences over the two forms and their attachment.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: فك رقبة أو أطعم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر ونافع وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r2.claim: These readers use the verbal noun إطعام alongside فك رقبة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر ونافع وحمزة: فك رقبة أو إطعام

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah says the person failed to cross the path in worldly life, then takes freeing a captive or feeding as its explanation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r5.anchor: أبو عبيدة: فلا اقتحم العقبة: فلم يقتحم العقبة في الدنيا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r6.claim: With the verbal-noun reading, an omitted اقتحام is required: otherwise the sentence equates the path itself with the event of freeing a captive, unlike the intended explanatory relation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p413/r6.anchor: لا بد من تقدير هذا المحذوف لأنه لا يخلو من أن تقدر

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r4.claim: The verbal reading may explain the challenge through its actions; an explanatory clause need not copy the nominal-predicate construction in other examples, and meaning can link the clauses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r4.anchor: ومن قال: فك رقبة أو أطعم في يوم ذي مسغبة [البلد/ 13، 14]، فإنه يجوز

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r1.claim: The preceding explanation says the Prophet addressed them directly and the Kufans justify an added alif by the closeness in meaning of the intensive and simple verb forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r1.anchor: دل بذلك على ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاطبهم به والحجة للكوفيين في زيادة الالف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r2.claim: With nominative endings, فك and إطعام are verbal nouns; with fatḥa they are past-tense verbs whose subject is the previously mentioned person, with رقبة and orphan accusatives.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r2.anchor: يقرآن بالرفع لانهما مصدران فالاول مضاف فحذف التنوين منه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r3.claim: On the verbal-noun reading, crossing the steep path means freeing a captive or feeding an orphan during famine, conditioned on faith.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p371/r3.anchor: فاقتحام العقبة وهي الصراط فك رقبة أو اطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة

QIRAAT-ER:90:13:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:90:13:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:90:13:1#1/r1.claim: The canonical syntactic variant changes the nominal freeing a neck into a finite verb with accusative object, he freed a neck.
QIRAAT-ER:90:13:1#1/r1.anchor: the nominal فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ (fakku raqabatin) becomes finite verb plus accusative object

QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r13.claim: Freeing a neck also means freeing oneself from the bondage of desire and people, with a guide leading from greed and humiliation into safety.
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r13.anchor: و { فك رقبة } هو إعتاق نفسه من رق الأغراض والأشخاص

QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r14.claim: Self-liberation entails leaving one's own planning and choice for the broad contentment of surrender.
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r14.anchor: بالتحرز من التدبير ، والخروج من ظلمات الاختيار إلى سعة الرضاء

SULAMI:v2p396/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p396/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p396/r1.claim: Freeing a neck means freeing oneself from four things: the self, one's deeds, seeing one's own merit, and seeking closeness.
SULAMI:v2p396/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : فك الرقاب من أربعة أشياء : من نفوسهم وأفعالهم ، ورؤية الفضل

SULAMI:v2p396/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p396/r2.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p396/r2.claim: Freeing a neck means freeing it from the humiliation of greed.
SULAMI:v2p396/r2.anchor: وقال القاسم : هو فك الرقاب من ذل الطمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p478/r4.claim: Fakk means freeing one thing from another; a poet uses it of releasing a captive from a shackle.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p482/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p482/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p482/r10.claim: Freeing the neck means releasing a person from captivity and bondage; a near relative combines charity with maintaining kinship ties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p482/r10.anchor: وفك الرقبة: تخليصها من الأسر والرق. ذا مقربة: ليجتمع صدقة وصلة

FARRA:v3p264/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p264/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p264/r1.claim: Arabic usually repeats lā across coordinated statements; here one lā covers the three parts of the steep path: freeing a slave or feeding during famine, then believing.
FARRA:v3p264/r1.anchor: ولم يضم إلى قوله: [فلا أقتحم] كلام آخر فيه (لا) لأن العرب لا تكاد تفرد (لا) في الكلام

FARRA:v3p264/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p264/r2.speaker: العوام
FARRA:v3p264/r2.claim: The common reading coordinates the verbal noun “freeing a slave” with “feeding.”
FARRA:v3p264/r2.anchor: وقد قرأ العوام: «فك رقبة (13) أو إطعام » (14)

FARRA:v3p264/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p264/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري وعلي بن أبي طالب
FARRA:v3p264/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read the nouns as a coordinated pair, فك رقبة أو إطعام.
FARRA:v3p264/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن البصري: «فك رقبة» وكذلك علي بن أبي طالب

FARRA:v3p265/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p265/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p265/r1.claim: The reading فك رقبة أو إطعام best fits Arabic because إطعام is a noun and should coordinate with another noun; ثم كان also supports this parse.
FARRA:v3p265/r1.anchor: «فك رقبة أو إطعام » وهو أشبه الوجهين بصحيح العربية لأن الإطعام: اسم، وينبغي أن يرد على الاسم اسم مثله،

FARRA:v3p265/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p265/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p265/r2.claim: The alternative reading is also possible if an omitted أن is supplied; a poem with أن in the second clause shows that it can be understood in the first.
FARRA:v3p265/r2.anchor: والوجه الآخر جائز تضمر فيه (أن) ، وتلقى [138/ ب] فيكون مثل قول الشاعر :

FARRA:v3p265/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p265/r3.speaker: شاعر
FARRA:v3p265/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses overt أن in the second coordinated clause, illustrating the elided أن in the earlier clause.
FARRA:v3p265/r3.anchor: ألا أيها ذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللذات هل أنت مخلدي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#7/r1.claim: Fakk raqaba means freeing a person from enslavement.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p528#7/r1.anchor: {فك رقبة} أي عتقها وفكها من الرق.

MAJAZ:v2p299/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p299/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p299/r5.claim: The obstacle is freeing a slave or feeding someone on a day of famine.
MAJAZ:v2p299/r5.anchor: «وما أدراك ما العقبة فك رقبة أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة» (12- 14) أي مجاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r1.claim: The question “what is the steep ascent?” magnifies the challenge; interpreting the ascent as emancipation is figurative identification, so there is no need to insert “crossing the ascent.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r1.anchor: تعظيم لشأن العقبة المفسرة بقوله سبحانه فك رقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r2.claim: One suggestion treats the ascent itself as gratitude because of its difficulty, but Alusi finds it unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم يحتمل أن يراد بالعقبة نفس الشكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reportedly calls the ascent a steep, slippery mountain in Hell; al-Hasan is reported to say the same.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن العقبة جبل زلال في جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to identify the ascent as Hell, or in another report as a barrier between Paradise and Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنها النار وفي رواية عبد بن حميد عنه أنها عقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r5.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Kalbi identify the ascent as the bridge over Hell; it may be the same as the reported barrier between Paradise and Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد والضحاك والكلبي أنها الصراط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r6.speaker: أبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r6.claim: Abu Rajaʾ says he heard that the ascent takes 7,000 years to climb and 7,000 years to descend; if these reports are sound, “crossing” and an implied noun must be supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي رجاء أنه قال بلغني أن العقبة التي ذكر الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r7.claim: If those locations are intended, iqtihām must mean passage across them and freeing a slave or feeding must count metaphorically as the cause of passage; Alusi will accept none as the verse's exegesis without a sound Prophetic report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#2/r7.anchor: أنا لا أقول بشيء من ذلك حتى تصح فيه تفسيرا للآية رواية مرفوعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r1.claim: Fakk is a verbal noun, as is fakkāk; the usual interpretation here is freeing an enslaved person from the status of slavery.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r1.anchor: وهو مصدر فك وكذا الفكاك بفتح الفاء كما نص عليه الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r2.claim: Al-Farra identifies fakkāk as a verbal noun alongside fakk.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r2.anchor: وكذا الفكاك بفتح الفاء كما نص عليه الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r3.speaker: البراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r3.claim: A report from al-Baraʾ begins with a Bedouin asking the Prophet for a deed that will admit him to Paradise; the Prophet advises freeing a person or contributing toward freeing a slave.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p137#3/r3.anchor: عن البراء رضي الله تعالى عنه أن أعرابيا قال يا رسول الله علمني عملا يدخلني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and the two grammarian-readers use past verbs fakka and atʿama with raqabatan in the accusative; on this reading fakk is an appositive of iqtahama, with intervening words parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والنحويان فك فعلا ماضيا رقبة بالنصب أو أطعم فعلا ماضيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r3.speaker: بعض التابعين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r3.claim: Some Successors read fakk raqabatin in construct and atʿama as a past verb, coordinated with the verbal noun by interpreting it verbally.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r3.anchor: وقرأ بعض التابعين فك رقبة بالإضافة أو أطعم فعلا ماضيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai read فك as a verb with ‘a neck’ as its object and ‘or he fed’ as a past verb; others read a noun phrase, ‘freeing a neck or feeding.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، والكسائي: "فك" بفتح الكاف، "رقبة" نصب، "أو أطعم" بفتح الهمزة والميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r3.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating a person, whose freedom becomes the emancipator’s ransom from the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r3.anchor: وأراد بفك الرقبة إعتاقها وإطلاقها، ومن أعتق رقبة كانت فداءه من النار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r4.claim: The Prophet says freeing a believing slave matches each bodily limb with a limb freed from the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "من أعتق رقبة مؤمنة أعتق الله بكل عضو منه عضوا من النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r5.speaker: البراء بن عازب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r5.claim: The Prophet distinguishes freeing a person outright from contributing to the purchase price; he also recommends a productive gift, helping a needy relative, feeding the hungry, giving water, enjoining right, and guarding one’s tongue if unable.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p432/r5.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال: جاء أعرابي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله علمني عملا يدخلني الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433/r1.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433/r1.claim: Ikrima interprets freeing a neck as freeing oneself from sins through repentance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433/r1.anchor: وقال عكرمة قوله: "فك رقبة"، يعني فك رقبة من الذنوب بالتوبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r3.claim: The pass is freeing a captive or feeding, during famine, a related orphan or impoverished person; repeated negation fits the multiple acts, and the terms mean hunger, kinship, and poverty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r3.anchor: وما أدراك ما العقبة فك رقبة أو إطعام فى يوم ذى مسغبة يتيما ذا مقربة

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī read فك رقبة أو أطعم as a substitute for اقتحم.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:10-16/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي « فك رقبة أو أطعم»على الإبدال من

BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.claim: The author rejects the need for allegorical explanations because the Qur’an itself answers its question by defining the obstacle through emancipation, feeding, faith, patience, and mercy.
BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.anchor: ونرى السياق في غير حاجة إلى تأويل يغنى عنه أن القرآن نفسه قد تول بيان

BINTSHATI:v1p186/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r1.claim: The sequence makes freeing an enslaved person the first step toward human dignity; broader social reform follows only after slavery’s dehumanizing injury is repaired.
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r1.anchor: تحرير الإنسانية من أغلال الرق هو أول خطوة في النضال الصعب

BINTSHATI:v1p186/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r3.claim: The author portrays Meccan injustice as desecrating the Prophet’s sanctuary while powerful owners enslave people and leave relatives and the poor hungry.
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r3.anchor: وأي شر أفدح وأوضح، من أن يستحل أذى الرسول في البلد الحرام؟

BINTSHATI:v1p186/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r4.claim: The surah calls people to struggle against slavery, class divisions, and social oppression by appealing to their innate capacity for moral effort.
BINTSHATI:v1p186/r4.anchor: القرآن إذ يدعو هنا إلى المجاهدة ضد الرق، والفروق الطبقية والظلم الإجتماعي

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.claim: The author takes thumma as real sequence: restoring dignity through emancipation and social justice through feeding are prerequisites for faith and its mutual exhortations.
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.anchor: عطف الإيمان، بلفظ: ثم، على ما قبله يبيح لنا أن نفهم

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.claim: The author rejects readings that detach faith from emancipation and feeding, arguing genuine faith requires resistance to tyranny, enslavement, and indifference to the poor.
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.anchor: لكن المفسرين عطلوا هذا الملحظ الجليل، بل عكسوا الوضع

BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.claim: The order makes human dignity and social justice grounds of faith; a society that accepts human enslavement and starvation cannot sustain sincere faith.
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.anchor: معلناً أن لا مكان لإيمان صادق مخلص، في مجتمع يسيغ عبودية بشر لغير خالقه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r4.speaker: البراء
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r4.claim: A report from al-Baraʾ distinguishes freeing a person outright from unlocking a neck by contributing toward its price.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r4.anchor: حديث البراء رضي الله عنه ( أعتق النسمة وفك الرقبة )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r5.claim: Breaking a neck’s bonds includes freeing someone from captivity, oppression, debt, or illness, as gratitude for God’s favor and love of excellence rather than display or expectation of reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p432/r5.anchor: أي من الأسر أو الظلم أو الغرم أو السقم شكرا لمن أولاه الخير

NAHHAS:v5p229/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p229/r11.claim: The steep path means freeing a slave or feeding someone on a day of hunger; Abū Hurayra reports that freeing a slave earns release from the Fire for each limb.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r11.anchor: التقدير اقتحام العقبة أن يفك رقبة كما روى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أعتق رقبة أعتق الله سبحانه بكل عضو منها عضوا منه من النار

NAHHAS:v5p229/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r12.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p229/r12.claim: With Abū Rajāʾ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, and al-Kisāʾī, he reads the words as verbal commands or past verbs: freeing a slave or feeding on a hungry day.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو وابن كثير والكسائي

NAHHAS:v5p229/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p229/r13.claim: He prefers the verbal reading because ثم كان is a past verb and should coordinate with another past verb.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r13.anchor: فاختار الفراء هذه القراءة واحتج بأن بعده ثم كان أي فلما عطف بكان وهي فعل ماض على الأول وجب أن يكون فك ليعطف فعلا ماضيا على فعل ماض

NAHHAS:v5p229/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r14.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v5p229/r14.claim: Al-Akhfash, Abū Ḥātim, and Abū ʿUbayd prefer the nominal reading.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r14.anchor: واختار الأخفش وأبو حاتم وأبو عبيد القراءة الأخرى

NAHHAS:v5p229/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p229/r15.claim: Both are sound readings and one may not attack the reading transmitted by the community; the past-verb coordination argument fails because it cannot coordinate by sense as proposed.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r15.anchor: الديانة تحظر الطعن على القراءة التي قرأ بها الجماعة ولا يجوز أن تكون مأخوذة إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد قال عليه السلام أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف فهما قراءتان حسنتان لا يجوز أن تقدم إحداهما على الأخرى فأما اعتراض الفراء بكان وبالنسق على الأول فلا يلزم

NAHHAS:v5p232/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p232/r1.claim: He allows the alternate reading by supplying an implied an and cites a poem; the author says the reading would then require an accusative and that an cannot be omitted without a substitute.
NAHHAS:v5p232/r1.anchor: ألا أيهذا اللائمي أحضر الوغى … وأن اشهد اللذات هل أنت مخلدي

NAHHAS:v5p232/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v5p232/r2.claim: He says the nominal ‘freeing a slave’ is the choice because it explains what the obstacle is.
NAHHAS:v5p232/r2.anchor: واعترض أبو عبيد فقال الاختيار فك رقبة لأنه يتبين للعقبة

NAHHAS:v5p232/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
NAHHAS:v5p232/r3.claim: He claims that every verse asking ‘what will make you know’ supplies an explanation, while ‘what makes you know’ does not.
NAHHAS:v5p232/r3.anchor: كل ما قال جل وعز وما أدراك فقد بينه

NAHHAS:v5p232/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p232/r4.claim: He rejects Sufyān's rule: the Qurʾān explains both the Calamity and the Reality after asking what they are.
NAHHAS:v5p232/r4.anchor: قال الله عز وجل ( وما أدراك

DURR-FULL:v8p523/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r4.claim: He identified the obstacle as Hell and said freeing a Muslim slave can ransom the freed person from the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن الحسن

DURR-FULL:v8p523/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r5.claim: He explained that the obstacle is scaled by freeing a slave; when asked which emancipation earns most, the Prophet answered: the most expensive.

DURR-FULL:v8p523/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r7.claim: After the passage was revealed, some proposed making dependent slave women prostitute themselves so their children could be freed; the Prophet forbade it and preferred even a whip given for God’s cause. Al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r7.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه والبيهقي في سننه عن عائشة

DURR-FULL:v8p523/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r8.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p523/r8.claim: She corrected a report attributed to Abu Hurayra: Muslims with no slave to free considered exploiting servant girls to free their children, but the Prophet forbade prostitution and preferred a whip spent for God.

DURR-FULL:v8p524/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r1.speaker: أبو نجيح السلمي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r1.claim: The Prophet said that freeing a slave saves the emancipator from the Fire limb by corresponding limb and bone by bone.
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي نجيح السلمي

DURR-FULL:v8p524/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r2.speaker: علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r2.claim: The Prophet said freeing a Muslim or believing person protects each corresponding limb of the emancipator from the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعد وابن أبي شيبة عن علي

DURR-FULL:v8p524/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r3.claim: Asked which slaves are best to free, the Prophet answered: those most expensive and most precious to their owners.

DURR-FULL:v8p524/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r4.speaker: البراء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r4.claim: The Prophet distinguished freeing a whole person from helping to emancipate one; when unable, he recommended helping kin, feeding the hungry, giving drink, enjoining good, or at least speaking only good.
DURR-FULL:v8p524/r4.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وابن حبان وابن مردويه والبيهقي عن البراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a rebuking question with its interrogative particle omitted: the boaster wasted wealth on gambling and wine, so why did he not spend generously on liberation and feeding during famine?
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r4.anchor: وتكون ( لا اقتحم العقبة ) استفهاما حذف منه أداته . وهو استفهام إنكار ، والمعنى : أنه يدعي إهلاك مال كثير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r5.claim: The single لا can negate the past without repetition because اقتحم entails the later acts of freeing and feeding, or because the later faith clause supplies the second negation; anything that prevents ambiguity can serve similarly, as an example from al-Ḥarīrī shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p355/r5.anchor: وقد جاءت هنا نافية في غير دعاء ، ولم تتكرر استغناء عن تكريرها بكون ما بعدها وهو { اقتحم العقبة } يتضمن شيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r3.claim: These readers pronounce فك and إطعام in the nominative; the clause explains the العقبة as freeing a person or feeding, with an omitted predicate, and the hard deed metaphor needs no added implied noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وخلف ، { فك رقبة } برفع { فك } وإضافته إلى { رقبة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r4.claim: They read فك as an active past verb with رقبة as its object and اطعم as another past verb; this explains the preceding negation or substitutes for اقتحم العقبة.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r4.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي { فك } بفتح الكاف على صيغة فعل المضي ، وبنصب { رقبة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r5.claim: فك is taking something from its possessor; رقبة uses the part for the whole person, especially a captive or slave whose neck is the first thing noticed because it is commonly shackled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p357/r5.anchor: من إطلاق اسم الجزء على كله مثل إطلاق رأس وعينن ووجه ، وإيثار لفظ الرقبة هنا لأن المراد ذات الأسير أو العبد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r1.claim: Freeing is an image for releasing a person from captivity or ownership, like pulling a difficult matter from a resistant holder's grasp.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r1.anchor: وأطلق الفك على تخليص المأخوذ في أسر أو ملك ، لمشابهة تخليص الأمر العسير بالنزع من يد القابض الممتنع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r2.claim: The verse is a foundational Islamic legal principle reflecting the Lawgiver's strong preference for human freedom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p358/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية أصل من أصول التشريع الإسلامي وهو تشوف الشارع إلى الحرية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485/r9.claim: If fakk is a past verb with accusative raqaba, fakk substitutes for iqtahama and explains it without an implied phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485/r9.anchor: وأما من قرأ «فك» على الفعل الماضي ونصب الرقبة، فليس يحتاج أن يقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r1.claim: Fakk al-raqaba means freeing a captive or enslaved person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r1.anchor: وترتيب هذه القراءات ووجوهها بينة، وفك الرقبة معناه: بالعتق من رقبة الأسر أو الرق،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r2.claim: A report promises that freeing a believing person earns release from the Fire for each corresponding limb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r2.anchor: من أعتق نسمة مؤمنة أعتق الله بكل عضو منها عضوا منه من النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r3.claim: Asked for a saving deed, a Bedouin is told that freeing a person is the great matter he seeks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r3.anchor: دلني على عمل أنجو به، فقال: «لئن قصرت القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r4.claim: The Prophet distinguishes freeing a person outright from contributing toward the price to free them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r4.anchor: «لا عتق النسمة أن تنفرد بعتقها، وفك الرقبة أن تعين في ثمنها» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r5.claim: The same distinction applies to a captive: direct release versus contributing to the ransom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وكذلك فك الأسير إن شاء الله، وفداؤه أن ينفرد الفادي به،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r6.claim: The Prophet also tells the Bedouin to be merciful to an unjust relative and, if unable, to restrain his tongue except for good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p485#2/r6.anchor: ثم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للأعرابي: «وأبق على ذي الرحمن الظالم، فإن لم تطق هذا كله، فكف لسانك إلا من خير»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو إلا عبد الوارث والكسائي والداجوني عن ابن ذكوان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135/r1.claim: They read fakku, with fatḥa on the kāf and raqabah in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبوه عمرو إلا عبد الوارث والكسائي والداجوني عن ابن ذكوان فك بفتح الكاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#2/r3.claim: Freeing a neck means releasing a person from bondage; anything released has been freed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#2/r3.anchor: معنى فك الرقبة تخليصها من أسر الرق وكل شيء أطلقته فقد فككته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r6.claim: Both readings, the noun phrase فك رقبة and the verbal فك رقبة, have closely similar meanings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r6.anchor: قرئ: {فك رقبة} بالإضافة، وقرئ على أنه فعل، وفيه ضمير الفاعل والرقبة مفعوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r7.claim: The Prophet says freeing a believing slave earns release from Hell limb for limb; Ali ibn al-Husayn frees a prized servant after Abu Hurayrah confirms the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن مرجانة: أنه سمع أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أعتق رقبة مؤمنة أعتق الله بكل إرب منها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, and Nasa'i transmit the Abu Hurayrah report, and Muslim says Zayn al-Abidin paid ten thousand dirhams for the freed servant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r8.anchor: وعند مسلم أن هذا الغلام الذي أعتقه علي بن الحسين زين العابدين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r9.claim: The Prophet says whoever frees a Muslim man or woman will have each of their bones matched by a bone freed from Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p405/r9.anchor: عن معدان بن أبي طلحة، عن أبي نجيح (5) قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "أيما مسلم أعتق رجلا مسلما،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r1.claim: Amr ibn Abasah reports that the Prophet promised a house in Paradise for building a mosque, release from Hell for freeing a Muslim, and light at resurrection for a white hair grown in Islam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن عبسة (7) أنه حدثهم: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من بنى مسجدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r2.claim: In another report to Sharhabil ibn al-Simt, Amr ibn Abasah says the Prophet described manumission as limb-for-limb rescue, and an arrow shot in God's path as equivalent to freeing an Ishmaelite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r2.anchor: قال عمرو: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "من أعتق رقبة مسلمة كانت فكاكه من النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r3.claim: A further Amr ibn Abasah report promises mercy and Paradise to parents whose three Muslim children die before maturity, and rewards white hair, an arrow, freeing a believer, and spending two items in God's path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r3.anchor: قال: سمعته يقول: "من ولد له ثلاثة أولاد في الإسلام فماتوا قبل أن يبلغوا الحنث،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir judges the chains of these Amr ibn Abasah reports good and strong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r4.anchor: وهذه أسانيد جيدة قوية، ولله الحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r5.claim: The Prophet tells Wathilah ibn al-Asqa that freeing a slave on behalf of a man who incurred Hell through murder can free each of the killer's limbs from Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p406/r5.anchor: قال: أتينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صاحب لنا قد أوجب -يعني النار-بالقتل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r1.claim: A report from Wathilah repeats that freeing a slave on behalf of the killer redeems a limb from Hell; Nasa'i transmits a version through another route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r1.anchor: وكذا رواه النسائي من حديث إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة، عن الغريف بن عياش الديلمي، عن واثلة، به (7)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r2.claim: The Prophet says that freeing a Muslim slave redeems the emancipator from the Fire; Ibn Kathir notes Ahmad alone transmits it by this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r2.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من أعتق رقبة مسلمة فهو فداؤه من النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r3.claim: A Bedouin asks how to enter Paradise; the Prophet distinguishes freeing a person outright from helping free one, then recommends a milk-bearing gift, supporting an unjust relative, feeding the hungry, watering the thirsty, commanding right, or guarding one's tongue.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p407/r3.anchor: فقال: "لئن كنت أقصرت الخطبة لقد أعرضت المسألة. أعتق النسمة، وفك الرقبة". فقال: يا رسول الله، أوليستا بواحدة؟ قال: "لا إن عتق النسمة

JISHUMI:v10p7422/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي والحسن وأبو رجاء العطاردي
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r1.claim: They read fakk as an active past verb with raqabatan as its object, or read aṭʿama as an active past verb “he fed.”
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي والحسن وأبو رجاء العطاردي: فك بنصب الكاف على فعل ماض

JISHUMI:v10p7422/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r2.claim: The other reading treats fakk raqabatin and iṭʿām as nouns; fakk is either linked to “he did not scale the steep path” or answers “what is the steep path?” as a nominal definition.
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: فك رقبة برفع الكاف رقبة بالكسر على الإضافة أو إطعام

JISHUMI:v10p7422/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء العطاردي
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r3.claim: They read dhā masghaba with accusative dhā as an object of feeding; the common reading makes dhī an adjective modifying the day.
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء العطاردي: ذا مسغبة يعني أطعم

JISHUMI:v10p7422/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r7.claim: Fakk is removing a restraint, like untying a knot or freeing a neck from slavery, or releasing a pledge.
JISHUMI:v10p7422/r7.anchor: والفك: فرق يزيل المنع كحل العقدة، وفك الغل والقيد

KASHSHAF:90:13/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:13/r1.claim: Freeing a neck means releasing it from slavery or another restraint.

KASHSHAF:90:13/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r2.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:90:13/r2.claim: The Prophet distinguishes emancipating someone outright from helping free them from retaliation or debt; this was his answer to a man's question about entering Paradise.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r2.anchor: أن تعين في تخليصها . من قود أو غرم

KASHSHAF:90:13/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:13/r3.claim: Emancipation and charity are among the most excellent deeds.

KASHSHAF:90:13/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF:90:13/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa holds emancipation more virtuous than charity.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r4.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : أن العتق أفضل من الصدقة

KASHSHAF:90:13/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r5.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
KASHSHAF:90:13/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions hold charity more virtuous than emancipation.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r5.anchor: وعند صاحبيه : الصدقة أفضل والآية أدل

KASHSHAF:90:13/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:13/r6.claim: The verse's ordering, naming emancipation before feeding, better supports Abu Hanifa's ranking.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r6.anchor: والآية أدل على قول أبي حنيفة لتقديم العتق الصدقة

KASHSHAF:90:13/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r7.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF:90:13/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says freeing a slave is better than giving surplus money to a relative, citing the Prophet's promise that God frees a limb from Fire for every limb released.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r7.anchor: أو يعتق رقبة ؟ قال : الرقبة أفضل

KASHSHAF:90:13/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r8.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:90:13/r8.claim: The Prophet says whoever frees a slave, God frees one of his limbs from the Fire for each limb of the slave.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r8.anchor: من فك رقبة فك الله بكل عضو منها عضواً منه من النار

KASHSHAF:90:13/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:13/r9.claim: One reading treats 'freeing a neck or feeding' as a nominal explanation: it is emancipation or feeding.
KASHSHAF:90:13/r9.anchor: على : هي فك رقبة ،   أو إطعام

KASHSHAF:90:13/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:13/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:13/r10.claim: Another reading uses the verb 'feed' as an alternative to 'free a neck,' parsing it as a substitute for 'climb the steep path.'
KASHSHAF:90:13/r10.anchor: أو أطعم ،   على الإبدال من اقتحم العقبة

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو، ابن كثير، الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r1.claim: Abu ‘Amr, Ibn Kathir, and al-Kisa’i read ‘fakka’ and ‘at‘ama’ as past-tense verbs with ‘raqabatan’ accusative; these verbs explain ‘iqtahama’.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير والكسائي " فك " فعلا ماضيا، " ورقبة " نصبا " أو أطعم " فعلا ماضيا

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r2.claim: The remaining readers take ‘fakku’ as a nominative noun with ‘raqabatin’ genitive and ‘it‘amun’ nominative; an implied topic means ‘it is freeing a slave or feeding’, with a permissive sense.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r2.anchor: والباقون " فك " برفع الكاف اسما، " رقبة

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r3.claim: An omitted noun, ‘iqtiham’, is required after ‘wa-ma adraka ma al-‘aqaba’ so the verbal noun ‘fakku’ explains a verbal noun rather than the concrete obstacle itself.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r3.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف مضاف دل عليه " فلا اقتحم " تقديره: وما أدراك ما اقتحام العقبة

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r4.speaker: أمير المؤمنين، أبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r4.claim: ‘Ali and Abu Raja’ read ‘fakka aw at‘ama’ as verbs but put ‘dha’ in the accusative; al-Hasan also has the accusative ‘dha’ with ‘it‘am’.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r4.anchor: وقرأ أمير المؤمنين وأبو رجاء " فك أو أطعم " فعلين كما تقدم، إلا أنهما نصبا " ذا " بالألف

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r5.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r5.claim: Al-Hasan reads ‘it‘am’ as a noun and ‘dha’ in the accusative; on these readings ‘dha’ is the object of feeding, with ‘yatiman’ appositional or adjectival.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن " إطعام " و " ذا " بالألف أيضا وهو على هاتين القراءتين مفعول " أطعم

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r6.claim: The common ‘dhi’ is an adjective of the day by metaphor: calling a day hungry intensifies the description, like calling a night standing or a day fasting; the agent of feeding is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r6.anchor: وهو في قراءة العامة " ذي " بالياء نعتا ل " يوم " على سبيل المجاز، وصف اليوم بالجوع مبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r7.claim: Omitting only the agent is one of the constructions Basran grammarians permit regularly; the author says he has treated the rule fully elsewhere.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r7.anchor: والفاعل لإطعام محذوف، وهذا أحد المواضع التي يطرد فيها حذف الفاعل وحده عند البصريين

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r8.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r8.claim: Al-Raghib defines masghaba as hunger with fatigue, sometimes thirst with fatigue; the related words come from roots for hunger, dust-poverty, and kinship.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r8.anchor: والمسغبة: الجوع مع التعب، وربما قيل في العطش مع التعب، قال الراغب

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari neatly groups masghaba, maqraba, and matraba as derived forms from hunger, closeness in kinship, and becoming poor.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r9.anchor: قال: " والمسغبة والمقربة والمتربة مفعلات من سغب إذا جاع وقرب في النسب وترب إذا افتقر

SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r10.claim: ‘Tariba’ means becoming so poor that the skin touches dust; ‘atraba’ with hamza instead means becoming wealthy, as in athra.
SAMIN-DURR:90:13/r10.anchor: يقال ترب، أي: افتقر حتى لصق جلده بالتراب. فأما أترب بالألف فبمعنى استغنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r10.claim: Freeing a neck may mean rescuing someone from captivity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r10.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : إخلاصها من الأسر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r11.claim: It may mean manumission; the enslaved person is likened to a captive bound at the neck, and freeing him to releasing a prisoner, as a line by Hassan ibn Thabit illustrates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r11.anchor: الثاني : عتقها من الرق , وسمي المرقوق رقبة لأنه بالرق كالأسير المربوط من رقبته ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r12.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r12.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's line witnesses the use of فك for releasing a captive.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p278/r12.anchor: كم من أسير فككناه بلا ثمن وجز ناصية كنأ مواليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r1.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r1.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports the Prophet saying that whoever frees a believing woman has thereby ransomed himself from the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r1.anchor: عقبة بن عامر الجهني أن النبي عليه السلام قال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r2.claim: Alternatively, freeing a neck may mean freeing one's own soul by avoiding sins and doing acts of obedience; al-Mawardi says this is closer to the correct interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r2.anchor: خلاص نفسه باجتناب المعاصي وفعل الطاعات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r7.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating a person from slavery or helping pay a slave's manumission contract.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r7.anchor: وفك الرقبة تخليصها من الرق والاعانة فى مال الكتابة

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r1.claim: Fakk al-raqabah means releasing someone from captivity, or from slavery; the cited hadith concerns helping with a manumission price.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r1.anchor: الأولى: قوله تعالى: { فك رقبة } فكها: خلاصها من الأسر. وقيل: من الرق.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r2.claim: Fakk is undoing a bond; the enslaved person is called a neck because slavery binds him like a captive, so manumission is release from bondage.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r2.anchor: والفك: هو حل القيد والرق قيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r3.speaker: حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r3.claim: His poem recalls freeing many captives without payment and cutting the forelock of those under their protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r3.anchor: كم من أسير فككناه بلا ثمن

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r4.speaker: عقبة بن عامر عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r4.claim: The Prophet says whoever frees a believing slave will have that slave as ransom from the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r4.anchor: من أعتق رقبة مؤمنة كانت فداءه من النار

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r5.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r5.claim: He offers another possible meaning: free one's own soul by avoiding sins and doing good deeds, which he considers closer to the correct sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r5.anchor: قال الماوردي: ويحتمل ثانيا أنه أراد فك رقبته وخلاص نفسه، باجتناب المعاصي، وفعل الطاعات

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r6.speaker: أصبغ
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r6.claim: He says freeing an expensive unbelieving slave is better than freeing an inexpensive believer, citing the report that the best manumission is the most costly.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r6.anchor: الرقبة الكافرة ذات الثمن أفضل في العتق من الرقبة المؤمنة القليلة الثمن

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r7.claim: He calls Asbagh's view mistaken: the hadith refers to a Muslim, and freeing a person for worship and pure monotheism matters more than minimizing cost.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r7.anchor: وما ذكره أصبغ وهلة، وإنما نظر إلى تنقيص المال

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r8.claim: Manumission and charity are among the best deeds; Abu Hanifa prefers manumission, while his two companions prefer charity, and the verse's order favors Abu Hanifa.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r8.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة: أن العتق أفضل من الصدقة. وعند صاحبيه الصدقة أفضل.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r9.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r9.claim: Asked whether to give surplus money to kin or free a slave, he chooses manumission, citing the report that God frees a limb from the Fire for each limb released.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:13/r9.anchor: من فك رقبة فك الله بكل عضو منها عضوا من النار

QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r1.claim: Freeing a slave may mean helping secure another’s manumission or personally emancipating them; either way, the result is the same.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r1.anchor: ورد أن فك الرقبة هو المشاركة في عتقها ، وأن العتق هو الاستقلال بهذا

QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r2.claim: The command came in Mecca while Muslims lacked a state, slavery was widespread, and converts faced severe abuse; emancipation was a way out, and Abu Bakr readily led this effort for God.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r2.anchor: وقد نزل هذا النص والإسلام في مكة محاصر

QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that Umayya tortured Bilal for his Islam, and Abu Bakr bought and emancipated him after finding him under torture.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r3.anchor: قال ابن اسحاق :  " وكان بلال مولى أبي بكر

QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Abu Bakr freed six other enslaved Muslims before the migration, with Bilal the seventh, including members of the families named in the account.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r4.anchor: ثم أعتق معه على الإسلام قبل أن يهاجر إلى المدينة ست رقاب . بلال سابعهم

QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق عن بعض أهله
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r5.claim: A relative reports that Abu Qahafa warned his son that freeing weak people would leave him without strong protectors; Abu Bakr replied that he acted only for God.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:13/r5.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : وحدثني محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي عتيق

RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r1.speaker: أبي حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa holds freeing a slave to be the best form of charity; this verse's placing emancipation before feeding supports him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r1.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة العتق أفضل أنواع الصدقات

RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r2.speaker: صاحبيه
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#3/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions hold that charity is better than emancipation.

STUDYQURAN:90:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r1.claim: A hadith says releasing a believing slave will ransom the emancipator from the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r1.anchor: A ḥadīth states, “Whoever releases a believing slave

STUDYQURAN:90:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r2.claim: There is debate over whether charity or manumission is more praiseworthy; some consider manumission superior because it comes first here.
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r2.anchor: There is a debate as to which is more praiseworthy, charity

STUDYQURAN:90:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r3.claim: Some read freeing a neck as freeing oneself through repentance.
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r3.anchor: This verse can also imply that one should free one’s own neck

STUDYQURAN:90:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r4.claim: Another reading takes freeing one's neck to mean performing worship to attain Paradise, the greatest freedom.
STUDYQURAN:90:13/r4.anchor: by performing the acts of worship by which one attains Paradise, since that is considered to be the greatest freedom

STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.claim: Good works in verses 13–16 must be grounded in belief, the necessary condition for their acceptance.
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.anchor: One does not assail the steep pass by simply performing the deeds mentioned in vv. 13–16; one must do so on the basis of belief

ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r1.speaker: Ikrimah and Razi
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r1.claim: Ikrimah, as cited by Baghawi, and Razi explain freeing a neck as freeing oneself from sin's burden.
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r1.anchor: Thus lkrimah, as quoted by Baghawi; also Razi.

ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r2.claim: Alternatively, fakk raqabah can mean freeing a human being from bondage, including social, economic, or political subjugation and exploitation describable as slavery.
ASAD-NOTES:90:11#n7/r2.anchor: Alternatively, the phrase fakk raqabah may be rendered as "the freeing of a human being from bondage"

TAB:90:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r1.speaker: author
TAB:90:13/r1.claim: Crossing the steep obstacle means freeing a person from slavery and the bonds of servitude.
TAB:90:13/r1.anchor: فقال :  اقتحامها وقطعها فكّ رقبة من الرقّ ،   وأسر العبودة

TAB:90:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB:90:13/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that freeing a Muslim slave serves as the emancipator's ransom from the Fire.
TAB:90:13/r2.anchor: ذُكر لنا أنه ليس مسلم يعتق رقبة مسلمة ،   إلا كانت فداءه من النار

TAB:90:13/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:90:13/r3.claim: Qatāda reports that the Prophet was asked which emancipation earns the greatest reward and answered: the most expensive.
TAB:90:13/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  وَما أدْرَاكَ ما الْعَقَبَةُ فَكّ رَقَبَةٍ ذُكر لنا أن نبيّ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سُئل

TAB:90:13/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:90:13/r4.claim: The Prophet says freeing a Muslim man or woman makes the emancipator's bones a ransom from the Fire, bone for bone.
TAB:90:13/r4.anchor: وأيّمَا امْرأةٍ مُسْلَمَةٍ أعْتَقَتْ امْرأةً مُسْلِمَةً ،   فإنّ اللّهَ جاعِلُ وَفاءَ كُلّ عَظْمٍ مِنْ عِظامِها

TAB:90:13/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:90:13/r5.claim: The Prophet says whoever frees a believing slave receives that slave as ransom from the Fire.
TAB:90:13/r5.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر الجُهَنيّ ،   أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :  «مَنْ أعْتَقَ رَقَبَةً مُؤْمِنَةً ،   فَهِيَ فِدَاؤُهُ مِنَ النّارِ »

TAB:90:13/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r6.speaker: قرّاء مكة وعامة قرّاء البصرة والكسائي
TAB:90:13/r6.claim: Meccan and most Basran readers, along with al-Kisāʾī, read the phrase as verbs: freeing a slave or feeding.
TAB:90:13/r6.anchor: فقرأه بعض قرّاء مكة وعامة قرّاء البصرة ،   عن ابن أبي إسحاق ،   ومن الكوفيين :  الكسائي :  «فَكّ رَقَبَةٍ أوْ أطْعَمَ »

TAB:90:13/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TAB:90:13/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr argues for the verbal reading because ثم كان implies that the person was already among believers, after neither freeing nor feeding.
TAB:90:13/r7.anchor: كأن معناه :  كان عنده ،   فلا فكّ رقبة ،   ولا أطعم ،   ثم كان من الذين آمنوا

TAB:90:13/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r8.speaker: عامة قرّاء المدينة والكوفة والشأم
TAB:90:13/r8.claim: Most Medinan, Kufan, and Syrian readers take فك رقبة as a genitive noun phrase and إطعام as a nominative verbal noun.
TAB:90:13/r8.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة والشأم فك رقبة على الإضافة أو إطعام على وجه المصدر

TAB:90:13/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r9.speaker: author
TAB:90:13/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both established readings as sound and their interpretations as intelligible.
TAB:90:13/r9.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك :  أنهما قراءتان معروفتان ،   قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القرّاء ،   وتأويل مفهوم

TAB:90:13/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r10.speaker: author
TAB:90:13/r10.claim: He prefers the verbal reading as smoother Arabic because it pairs verbs with verbs and nouns with nouns, matching ثم كان.
TAB:90:13/r10.anchor: والعرب تُؤْثِر ردّ الأسماء على الأسماء مثلها ،   والأفعال على الأفعال

TAB:90:13/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r11.speaker: author
TAB:90:13/r11.claim: The noun reading remains possible by eliding أن before a verb, as in Ṭarafa's poetic construction.
TAB:90:13/r11.anchor: كما قال طرفة بن العبد :  ألا أيّهاذا الزّاجري أحْضُرَ الْوَغَى *** وأنْ أشْهَدَ اللّذّاتِ هَلْ أنتَ مُخْلِدي

TAB:90:13/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:13/r12.speaker: author
TAB:90:13/r12.claim: On the noun reading, freeing or feeding explains what the obstacle is, like the answer that the Hawiya is a burning fire.
TAB:90:13/r12.anchor: وإذا وُجّه الكلام إلى هذا الوجه كان قوله :  فَكّ رَقَبَةٍ أوْ إطْعامٌ تفسيرا لقوله :  وَما أدْرَاكَ ما الْعَقَبَةُ

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r1.claim: The catalogue of virtues has biblical roots and belongs to the prophetic call to support orphans and the poor, with parallels noted at 107:2–3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Tugendkatalog ist offensichtlich biblisch geprägt (zum prophetischen Topos der gebotenen Unterstützung von Waisen und Armen s. allg. die Anmerkung zu 107:2–3

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r2.claim: The catalogue clearly echoes Isaiah 58:6–7: freeing slaves, feeding the hungry, housing the poor, clothing the naked, and helping kin.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Auch in der Jesaja-Stelle antwortet der Tugendkatalog auf eine Frage, allerdings nicht die nach dem „steilen Weg“, sondern nach einem „Fasten …, das dem Herrn gefällt“

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r3.claim: Both the Qur'anic and Isaiah catalogues begin with freeing slaves and then identify poor people and relatives as recipients of aid, though their framing questions differ.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:13-16:anmerkung/r3.anchor: wie im Koran steht auch in der Bibelstelle die Befreiung von Sklaven am Anfang, und wie im Koran werden daraufhin u. a. Arme und Verwandte als Empfänger von Hilfeleistungen hervorgehoben

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:1-4:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:1-4:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:1-4:kommentar/r3.claim: The verse presents Mecca as a place of ordinary social life as well as ritual, dependent on support for vulnerable people; religious norms therefore extend beyond worship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:1-4:kommentar/r3.anchor: Offenbar soll der Vers aber gerade betonen, dass der Wallfahrtsort Mekka nicht nur ein Schauplatz sakraler Vollzüge ist, sondern auch ein Ort profanen menschlichen Zusammenlebens

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r3.claim: After a negative example, the text calls for wealth to be used to care for vulnerable people rather than for self-aggrandizement, imitating God's care for humanity.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r3.anchor: Anstelle einer letzten Endes nur der Selbsterhöhung dienenden Besitzverschwendung wird dazu angehalten, Besitz zur gezielten Fürsorge für schwächere und notleidende Mitmenschen einzusetzen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r4.claim: The virtue list adapts Isaiah 58:5–7 in a different context: Isaiah critiques merely external ritual, whereas the Qur'an grounds moral duty in God's grace to all humanity.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r4.anchor: In Jesaja 58:5–7 – wo im Gegensatz zum Koran nur das Volk Israel

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.claim: The biblical allusion overwrites the heroic worldview carried by the poetry cited in verse 6, making scripture an ally against the values of canonical pre-Islamic verse.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die durch die Anspielung in V. 90:6 repräsentierte Dichtung und das von ihr transportierte heroische Weltbild werden durch eine – vielleicht aus gottesdienstlichen Lesungen vertraute – Bibel-Referenz überschrieben

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r7.claim: The biblically inspired but deliberately Arabized virtue list culminates the sura and spells out the normative consequences of creation and God's care.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r7.anchor: Der biblisch inspirierte, in literarischer Hinsicht jedoch gezielt arabisierte Tugendkatalog stellt damit den Kulminationspunkt der gesamten Sure dar

TABATABAI:90:10-17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r6.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating a slave; alternatively the obstacle itself is emancipation, so climbing it is performing that very act. This rejects an interpretation requiring an omitted word for “climbing.”
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r6.anchor: هي أي العقبة فك رقبة فالمراد بالعقبة نفس الفك الذي هو العمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p243/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p243/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p243/r2.claim: Al-Balad comprehensively presents the elements of a message: Mecca, its resident Messenger, humanity as recipients, faith and good works as the message, and believers and disbelievers as the two response groups.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p243/r2.anchor: استوفت عناصر البلاغ والإرسال، فقد ذكرت موطن الرسالة، والرسول

TABRISI:90:13-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:13-14/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads labadan with gemination; the other readers pronounce it lightly.
TABRISI:90:13-14/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر لبدا بالتشديد والباقون بالتخفيف

TABRISI:90:1-20/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20/r2.claim: For the anomalous ذا مسغبة reading, orphan can substitute for it; alternatively, orphan describes a day of hunger by following an adjective used substantivally.
TABRISI:90:1-20/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ ذا مسغبة جعله مفعول إطعام ويتيما بدل منه ويجوز أن يكون يتيما وصفا

TABRISI:90:1-20/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20/r11.claim: Fakk means removing a restraint so that an action previously prevented becomes possible; freeing a neck ends enslavement and establishes liberty.
TABRISI:90:1-20/r11.anchor: والفك فرق يزيد المنع ويمكن معه أمر لم يكن متمكنا كفك القيد والغل

TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r1.claim: Fakk al-raqabah can mean freeing a person from sins through repentance.
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r1.anchor: إن معنى فك رقبة أن يفك رقبة من الذنوب بالتوبة عن عكرمة

TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r2.claim: Another interpretation is freeing oneself from punishment by accepting the burden of obedience.
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r2.anchor: أراد فك نفسه من العقاب بتحمل الطاعات عن الجبائي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r4.claim: The ascent is then explained as freeing a slave or feeding someone in need.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r4.anchor: ثم فسر العقبة بعد ذلك بقوله: {فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ * أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r5.claim: The Prophet distinguishes freeing a slave outright from helping release someone facing retaliation or debt; a man had asked for a deed leading to Paradise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r5.anchor: أن رجلاً قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: دُلّني على عمل يُدخلني الجنة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r6.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r6.claim: Fakk is literally untying a restraint; a slave is called a neck because enslavement makes him like a captive bound by the neck.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p270/r6.anchor: والفك في الأصل حل القيد، سمي العتق فكاً، لأن الرق كالقيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p271/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p271/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p271/r1.claim: The wording freeing a neck evokes the enslaved person's severe distress and suffering, among the harshest forms of human toil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p271/r1.anchor: واختيار هذا التعبير يوحي بشدة حال المسترق، وكربه ومعاناته ومكابدته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r1.claim: Aw marks alternatives rather than requiring all duties together: feeding either needy class, separately or in combination, suffices for the intended variety.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r1.anchor: بل المراد التنويع. والمقصود أن يطعم هذه الأصناف من الناس، اليتيم أو المسكين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r2.claim: Freeing slaves precedes feeding to signal the importance Islam gives to liberating people from bondage.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r2.anchor: وقد قدم فك الرقاب على إطعام اليتامى والمساكين إشارة إلى عظم الحرية في الإسلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r3.claim: The enslaved, hungry, orphaned, and destitute are among those who endure the greatest toil; liberating and feeding them enact mercy, while they need patience.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r3.anchor: فهؤلاء من أشد الناس مكابدة ومعاناه. ثم انظر إلى ارتباط هؤلاء الأصناف بقوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.claim: The man who boasts of wasting much money spent it in the wrong place, since he neither fed a hungry person nor freed anyone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r4.anchor: فقد أهلكها هذا القائل في غير محلها، فلم يطعمْ جائعاً ولم يفكَّ رقبة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.claim: The surah's hardships call for patience: choosing either path, climbing the ascent, serving the enslaved, enduring famine, and caring for orphans and the destitute all demand perseverance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.anchor: وسلوك النجدين يحتاج إلى صبر لما في صعودهما وسلوكهما من تعب ونَصَب، واقتحام العقبة يحتاج إلى صبر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.claim: The boastful spender needs mercy so he directs his wealth to the needy instead of wasting it uselessly; the enslaved person also needs compassion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.anchor: وهذا الذي أهلك مالاً لُبداً، يحتاج إلى الرحمة لينفق المال على ذوي الحاجة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r4.claim: Freeing a neck can include manumission or releasing someone from financial claims and debts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r4.anchor: يحتمل العتق وغيره من فك المغارم والديون وغيرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r4.claim: Freeing a neck means releasing someone from slavery or another binding constraint, as in releasing a pledge or opening a sealed book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r4.anchor: وفك الرقبة: تخليصها من إسار الرق، وفك الرهن، وفكاكه: تخليصه من غلق الرهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r5.claim: Fakk is separation that removes a restraint, as when a chain is broken and a person is separated from enslavement through emancipation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r5.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: الفك فرق يزيل المنع، كفك القيد والغل، وفك الرقبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r6.claim: As a verbal noun, fakka yafukkuha takes fatḥa in fakākan, not kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p27/r6.anchor: قال الفراء في المصادر: فكها يفكها فكاكا، بفتح الفاء في المصدر، ولا تقل بكسرها

WAHIDI-QT:90:13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:13/r1.claim: Freeing a slave means helping pay the price for the slave's emancipation.
WAHIDI-QT:90:13/r1.anchor: وهو إخراجها من الرق بالعون في ثمنها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r1.claim: Fakk raqabah means releasing any restraint, not only manumitting a slave; Qur'anic expiation uses the narrower word taḥrīr, while fakk also covers freeing a debtor or someone wanted for another matter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r1.anchor: فك رقبة تعني تخليصها من الرق كالغارم والمطلوب لأمر ما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r2.claim: The image applies across eras to oppressed peoples and to relations in which individuals or rulers subjugate others; social liberation remains a lasting need.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r2.anchor: فك الرقبة هي عقبة من عقبات المجتمع قديماً وحديثاً ومستقبلاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r3.claim: The broader sense keeps the verse applicable in every age and society, including aid to oppressed populations and relief from forms of personal or governmental coercion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p399/r3.anchor: فلا يمكن أن تأتي آية في القرآن ولا يكون لها تطبيق لكل زمان ومكان

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r2.claim: “Neck” is a part-for-whole metaphor for a person, especially a slave; releasing a neck means freeing an enslaved person, with freeing a slave as the simplest example.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r2.anchor: “rakabe” boyun demek olup zikr-i cüz irâde-i kül tarîkiyle mecaz olarak zat ve şahıs mânasında müte‘âreftir

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r3.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever frees a believing slave has each of his own limbs freed from Hell in return for the corresponding limb, down to the private parts; it is transmitted in major hadith collections.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r3.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Tirmizî ve sâirede Ebû Hüreyre radıyallahu anh’tan mervîdir

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r4.speaker: Berâ’
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r4.claim: A Bedouin asked for a deed leading to Paradise; the Prophet distinguished freeing a person by oneself from helping to manumit a slave, saying the latter is broader and may be shared.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r4.anchor: İmam Ahmed ve İbn Hibban ve İbn Merdûye ve Beyhakī, Berâ’ radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r5.claim: If freeing one person is such a virtue, freeing an entire people or community is an even greater act of courage.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r5.anchor: Bir ferdi hürriyete kavuşturmak böyle büyük bir fazilet ve kahramanlık olunca bir kavmin, bir cemaatin hürriyetini kurtarmak

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r6.claim: A second meaning is rescuing oneself from Hell through righteous deeds, since each person is held by what he has earned; this requires struggle against the commanding soul and Satan.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r6.anchor: her nefsin halâsı kazancına bağlı olduğu için insanın a‘mâl-i sâliha kesbiyle kendisini cehennem azâbından kurtarması demektir

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r7.claim: The failure of the proud person to overcome the ascent reflects his failure to struggle against his lower desires and Satan’s temptations.
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r7.anchor: nefs-i emmârenin azgın hevâlarıyla Şeytan’ın iğvâlarına karşı mücahede etmekle olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.claim: The era's gravest human problems were slavery, poverty, and lack of mercy; remedies were freeing slaves, feeding orphans and the poor, and urging patience and compassion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.anchor: o dönemin en ağır insanî sorunları kölelik, yoksulluk ve merhametsizlikti. O dönem için çareler ise köleleri özgürlüklerine kavuşturmak, yetimi ve yoksulu doyurmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.claim: This summary of Islamic social ethics gives examples rather than an exhaustive or restrictive list of good works.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.anchor: İslâm’ın sosyal ahlâkının kapsamlı bir özeti olan bu ifadeler, eski deyimiyle tahdîdî değil tâdâdîdir; yani sınırlayıcı değil, örnek göstericidir

AKHFASH:v2p579/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p579/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p579/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash rejects an alternative construal and prefers the direct fakk raqaba phrase as the good reading.
AKHFASH:v2p579/r3.anchor: وليس هذا بذاك و {فك رقبة} هو الجيد

AKHFASH:v2p579/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p579/r4.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p579/r4.claim: Some gave a different syntactic construal of fakk raqaba in relation to the obstacle and the following or feeding phrase.
AKHFASH:v2p579/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فك رقبة} وليس هذا بذاك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r3.claim: Failing to scale the steep path means failing to thank God through righteous deeds, freeing slaves, feeding the needy, and foundational faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r3.anchor: يعني : فلم يشكر تلك الأيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r9.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating it from bondage or otherwise releasing it from an obligation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r9.anchor: وفك الرقبة : تخليصها من رق أو غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r10.claim: The Prophet distinguishes emancipation from helping free someone from retaliation or debt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r10.anchor: إعتاقها أن تنفرد بعتقها . وفكها : أن تعين في تخليصها من قود أو غرم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r11.claim: Abu Hanifa considers emancipation superior to charity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r11.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : أن العتق أفضل من الصدقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r12.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r12.claim: Al-Shabi says freeing a slave is better than giving surplus funds to a relative, citing the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r12.anchor: وعن الشعبي في رجل عنده فضل نفقة : أيضعه في ذي قرابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever frees a neck will have every corresponding limb freed from the Fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r1.anchor: من فك رقبة فك الله بكل عضو منها عضوا منه من النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r2.claim: One reading treats freeing or feeding as nominal predicates; another reads the verbs as substitutes explaining the obstacle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760/r2.anchor: قرىء : ( فك رقبة ) أو إطعام ) على : هي فك رقبة

RAZI-FULL:v31p167/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p167/r7.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p167/r7.claim: Al-Wahidi objects that people have not crossed Hell's obstacle, making that interpretation obvious; the following verse explains it as freeing a slave and feeding someone.
RAZI-FULL:v31p167/r7.anchor: قال الواحدي : وهذا تفسير فيه نظر

RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r1.claim: Fakk is release from a restrictive bond; freeing a neck removes the legal status of slavery, like releasing a fetter or pledge.
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r1.anchor: الفك فرق يزيل المنع كفك القيد والغل

RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p168#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra says the verbal noun is fakāk, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, not kasra.
